displayedInputs.question: Are complementary events always mutually exclusive?
Are mutually exclusive events always complementary?

choices.C: Always in the classical probability model
choices.D: Only when there are two sample points is this not necessarily true

displayedInputs.question: \(P(A)=0.3\). If \(B\) is the complement of \(A\), what is \(P(B)\), expressed as a fraction? \(0.3=3/10\).
A sample space has 6 equally likely outcomes. How many outcomes do the events “the number shown is 1” and “the number shown is 2” contain altogether?
\(A\) and \(B\) are independent, with \(P(A)=1/2\) and \(P(B)=1/3\). What is \(P(A\cap B)\)?

A coin is tossed twice independently. The probability of heads on the first toss is \(1/2\), and the probability of heads on the second toss is \(1/2\). What is the probability of heads on both tosses?
If neither \(A\) nor \(B\) is an impossible event, and they are mutually exclusive, which statement holds?
What does independence mean?

choices.A: Whether one event occurs does not change the probability of the other
choices.B: The two events cannot occur simultaneously
choices.C: The two events must occur simultaneously
choices.D: The sum of the probabilities is 1

displayedInputs.question: The probability of a hit on each shot is \(1/2\). What is the probability of hits on all 3 independent shots?
The probability of a miss on each shot is \(1/2\). What is the probability of misses on all 3 shots?
The probability of a hit on a single shot is \(1/2\). The complement of at least 1 hit is misses on all 3 shots. What is the probability of at least 1 hit in 3 independent shots?
Does calculating with the complement of “at least once” here involve conditional probability?

choices.C: We must first know that the first shot was a hit
choices.D: Only the classical probability model does not require it

displayedInputs.question: In 200 trials, an event occurred 40 times. What is its relative frequency?
Another 100 trials were conducted, and the event occurred 20 times. What is its relative frequency in this batch?
What does a relative frequency stabilizing around \(1/5\) indicate?

choices.A: The probability has already become the next value of the relative frequency
choices.B: The probability can be estimated as \(1/5\)
choices.C: The event will definitely occur on the next trial
choices.D: The trials can stop, and the result will no longer change

displayedInputs.question: What is the difference between relative frequency and probability?

choices.B: Relative frequency can be greater than 1
choices.C: Relative frequency comes from trials already conducted, while probability describes the underlying regularity of the event itself
choices.D: Probability changes with the number of trials

displayedInputs.question: An event occurred 320 times in 1000 trials. What is the probability estimated using relative frequency?
In another run, only 10 trials were conducted, and the event occurred 8 times. What is its relative frequency in these 10 trials?
For the same experiment, which estimate is usually more reliable?

choices.A: The one with the higher relative frequency

displayedInputs.question: If the estimated probability is \(1/4\), approximately how many occurrences are expected in 40 trials?
Which of the following matches the meaning of a vector in space?

choices.A: A quantity with length only and no direction
choices.B: A quantity with both magnitude and direction
choices.C: A point with position only and no magnitude
choices.D: A line segment with no direction indicated

displayedInputs.question: \(a=(1,0,0)\), \(b=(2,0,0)\). The two vectors have the same direction. How many times \(|a|\) is \(|b|\)?
What is the magnitude of the zero vector?

choices.B: Equal to the magnitude of any nonzero vector

displayedInputs.question: \(A(0,0,0)\), \(B(0,3,0)\). What is the \(y\)-coordinate of the vector corresponding to the directed line segment \(AB\)?
\(a=(1,0,2)\), \(b=(3,4,−1)\). What is the x-coordinate of \(a+b\)?
\(a=(2,−1,4)\), \(b=(2,3,1)\). What is the z-coordinate of \(a−b\)?
\(a=(1,−2,3)\). What is the y-coordinate of \(3a\)?
Which rule can be used for adding vectors in space?

choices.A: Only multiplying all the coordinates together
choices.B: The triangle rule or parallelogram rule
choices.C: It can only be used for coplanar zero vectors
choices.D: Adding two vectors must give the zero vector

displayedInputs.question: What does it mean if the dot product of two nonzero vectors in space equals 0?

choices.C: The two vectors have equal magnitudes
choices.D: Both vectors must be zero vectors

displayedInputs.question: If \(a\cdot b>0\) and neither \(a\) nor \(b\) is a zero vector, what is the angle between them?
\(a=(1,0,2)\), \(b=(2,0,4)\). What is the geometric relationship between these two vectors?
\(a=(1,2,k)\) and \(b=(2,4,6)\) are collinear. What is \(k\)?
Is the zero vector collinear with every vector in space?

choices.B: It is collinear only with unit vectors
choices.D: It is collinear only on the coordinate axes
